findings.explanation: high confidence. In Claim 7 (paragraph [p6-1]), the argument contains multiple fatal errors. First, it claims: 'Recall, for each i, that N^{Int}(Y_i) contains non-adjacent vertices that lie in J_m; call such a pair z_i' and z_i''.' However, J_m is merely an independent set of size k in G_{P_{Big}}; there is no guarantee that J_m contains any vertices, let alone two non-adjacent vertices, in each N^{Int}(Y_i) (indeed, if a > k/2, J_m cannot contain two vertices from each). Second, the induction assumes that the token on y_1' has already been moved off, but sigma was a reconfiguration sequence in G, not G', and the proof provides no valid vertex in G' to which the token on y_1' can be moved. Third, in the base case, moving the token on y_1'' to z_1' requires z_1' to have no adjacent tokens, but z_1' is adjacent to both vertices in Y_1 = {y_1', y_1''}; if the token on y_1' has not been properly removed to a non-neighbor, this jump is illegal. Fourth, for the induction step, to move a token from y_i' to z_{i-1}'', z_{i-1}'' must not have any token on its neighbors, but z_{i-1}'' is in N^{Int}(Y_{i-1}) and nothing ensures that y_i' can jump to z_{i-1}'' without violating independence of the configuration or that z_{i-1}'' was unoccupied and available. Witness: J_m has size k, so for a > k/2, it is impossible for J_m to contain two vertices in N^{Int}(Y_i) for each i in {1, ..., a}.

evidence.text: Instead assume that \( z_s \in \cup_{Y \in P^2} C_Y \). By our construction of \( G' \), since \( z_s \notin V(G') \), we know \( z_s \in \cup_{Y \in P_{\mathrm{Big}}} N^{\mathrm{Int}}(Y) \). Denote \( P_{\mathrm{Big}} \cap P^2 \) by \( \{Y_1, \ldots, Y_a\} \) in an arbitrary order (for some integer \( a \)), and denote \( Y_i \) by \( \{y_i', y_i''\} \) for each \( i \in \{1, \ldots, a\} \). Since \( \sigma \) moves a token to \( z_s \), at some (earlier) point \( \sigma \) moves a token off of some vertex in some \( Y_i \). By symmetry, assume \( \sigma \) first moves a token off of \( y_1' \). We show, by induction on \( i \), that we can move all tokens off of \( \cup_{i=1}^a Y_i \). Recall, for each \( i \), that \( N^{\mathrm{Int}}(Y_i) \) contains non-adjacent vertices that lie in \( J_m \); call such a pair \( z_i' \) and \( z_i'' \). For the base case, we move the token on \( y_1'' \) to \( z_1' \). For the induction step, we assume that no token appears on the closed neighborhood of \( z_{i-1}'' \). So we move a token from \( y_i' \) to \( z_{i-1}'' \) and then we move a token from \( y_i'' \) to \( z_i' \). This finishes the induction proof.
